draft.title: Draft — must be reviewed before publication
draft.body: This privacy policy is a working draft for the application currently being built. The controller details are binding; the description of the processing follows the current state of the code. Before this site goes public, the board, as the association's legal representative, has to review this text and have it signed off legally.
draft.openQuestions: One question outranks the rest: when a club organises an event of its own on this platform, it is undetermined whether the association is the sole controller, a processor for that club, or a joint controller with it — and each answer demands different agreements. That and every other undecided point — retention periods, the deletion concept and the consent for position data, the question of a data protection officer — is marked as an open question below and deliberately not guessed at.

sections.heading: Dispute resolution
paragraphs: We are neither obliged nor willing to take part in dispute resolution proceedings before a consumer arbitration board.
The formerly mandatory reference to the European Commission's online dispute resolution platform no longer applies: that ODR platform was shut down in July 2025.

sections.heading: Liability for content
paragraphs: As a service provider we are responsible for our own content on these pages under the general laws. We are not obliged to monitor third-party information transmitted or stored here, nor to investigate circumstances that point to unlawful activity (§§ 7 to 10 DDG). As soon as we become aware of a specific infringement, we remove the content concerned without delay.
Results, standings and race data are recorded to the best of our knowledge. Only the result published by the race committee of the respective event is authoritative.

sections.heading: Liability for links
paragraphs: Our pages link to external sites whose content is outside our control. The respective provider is always responsible for that content. No unlawful content was apparent when the links were created; without concrete grounds for suspicion, permanent monitoring of linked content is not reasonable.

sections.heading: Copyright
paragraphs: Texts, result lists and standings that we publish on these pages may be used freely, including commercially, under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence (CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) — name the source “Deutsche Segel-Liga e.V.” and, online, link to the page. This includes our news and press releases.
Not covered: photographs remain the work of the photographers credited with them, and club crests and logos the property of their clubs. Their rights are not ours to grant; ask the rights holder.

sections.heading: Scope of this policy
paragraphs: This policy explains what personal data this website and the tools behind it process, and on what basis. The website is operated by Deutsche Segel-Liga e.V.

It is used in several ways: visitors read public pages without an account; sailors and club officials sign in to maintain squads, profiles, waivers and expense claims; the race committee enters results; the editorial team publishes news, press releases and pictures; and a club can organise an event of its own here. What we process depends on which of these applies to you.

sections.heading: Controller
paragraphs:
Deutsche Segel-Liga e.V.
c/o Düsseldorfer Yacht-Club
Rotterdamer Straße 30
40474 Düsseldorf
Germany

Authorised representatives: the board (see the legal notice)
Email: vorstand@deutsche-segelliga.de
Legal notice: https://www.deutsche-segelliga.de/legal-notice
We have not appointed a data protection officer: the association is not obliged to (Art. 37 GDPR, § 38 BDSG). For any question about your data, write to the board at the address above.

sections.heading: Who is responsible when a club runs its own event
paragraphs: A club can use this website to organise an event of its own that belongs to none of the association's series — a cup, a training weekend. For such an event, the host club is the controller of the participants' data: it decides who takes part, collects the entries, crews and waivers, and publishes the results. The association provides the website and processes that data on the club's behalf (Art. 28 GDPR). Address your rights concerning such an event to the host club named on the event's page.
For the events of the association's own series — even where a club hosts an act — and for everything across events (accounts, people, profiles, standings), Deutsche Segel-Liga e.V. is the controller.
sections.open: The data processing agreement a host club accepts before running its own event here, and naming the host club as controller on the event's page, are decided but not built yet.

sections.heading: Categories of data we process
paragraphs: Depending on how you use the website:
items: Account data: email address, display name, whether that address has been verified, and the time of your last sign-in.
Sign-in data: which method you use (Google, Microsoft, a code by email, or a password) and the provider's identifier for you; one-time codes and passwords, stored only as hashes.

Person data: first and last name, date of birth, optionally an email address and a federation (DSV) number, whether the profile page is public, and a profile photo. A club may record a person who has no account — a child, a crew member who never signs in.

Membership and role data: which clubs you are a member of, and what you are to each club, series and event (for example manager, admin, race officer, jury, helper, treasurer, editor); for a parent, the link as guardian of a child.
Sporting data: squad and lineup entries, boat assignments, and race results per team.

Waiver records: which version of the waiver text was confirmed, when, in which language, by which method, from which account, the browser identifier of that confirmation, and for minors the guardian's name and the scan of their signed form.
Money: expense claims with their items and receipts, the name and IBAN of the account they are paid to, decisions on them, and payments; your saved bank account (holder, IBAN, BIC).
Personal documents you upload yourself: licences and certificates, with their kind, title and expiry date.
Editorial content: posts with the author's name as written, and pictures with the photographer's credit.
Technical data: the IP address your device uses to reach the site, the time and the address requested, in the server's request log.

sections.heading: Why we process it
paragraphs: The purposes are those of running a sailing league and its website:
items: Running the competition: registrations, squads, lineups, pairing lists, results and standings.
Publishing sporting results and who took part, and news, press releases and pictures about the regattas.
Sign-in and access control, so that only the right people can see and change data.
Documenting liability waivers as evidence that they were given.
Reimbursing expenses: deciding claims and paying them to the right account.
Letting a club's or an event's organisers check the licences of the people working for them.
Security, troubleshooting, and meeting statutory retention duties where they apply.

sections.heading: Legal bases
paragraphs: We process personal data on the following bases under the GDPR:

Alongside the GDPR, German national rules apply, in particular the Federal Data Protection Act (BDSG), which contains its own provisions on access, erasure, objection, special categories of data and automated decision-making. State data protection laws may apply as well.
items: Consent, Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR — where we ask for it specifically, in particular for the position tracking that is planned but not yet in use.
Contract and membership, Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR — reimbursing the expenses of those who work for a club or an event, and membership of a club.
Legitimate interests, Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR — operating and securing the site, running the competition, and publishing sporting results and participation.
Legal obligation, Art. 6(1)(c) GDPR — where commercial or tax law requires records to be kept.
sections.open: The basis for publishing sailors' names, club affiliation and photos openly on the internet — legitimate interest or consent — is a genuine legal judgment and has not been settled. It needs review by the association's legal advisers, especially for participants under 18, whose names are currently public in exactly the same way as an adult's.

sections.heading: Security measures
paragraphs: We take technical and organisational measures appropriate to the risk, and consider data protection when choosing and building the software itself. In particular:
items: Identity comes from Google, Microsoft, a one-time code sent by email, or a password you chose to set. A password is stored only as an Argon2id hash — never in readable form — and an account locks for a growing period after five wrong attempts.
One-time codes are stored only as an Argon2 hash, expire after ten minutes, allow five attempts, and can be used once.
All traffic runs over HTTPS (TLS).
Permissions are checked against the database on every single request, so withdrawing one takes effect immediately rather than at the next sign-in.

Waiver scans, receipts and personal documents are stored under random names, never at a public address, and are delivered only through one endpoint each that checks who asks. Every look at a waiver scan is logged, and so is every look at someone else's receipt or document.

Profile photos and the pictures shown on the site are re-encoded, which removes the original metadata — including any location the camera recorded. The editorial picture library keeps the uploaded original, with its metadata, privately and never shows it.
A minor's profile photo is not served publicly at all (see below).

sections.heading: Recipients and processors
paragraphs: We use service providers who process data on our behalf. They are bound by our instructions and may not use the data for their own purposes. The files uploaded here — photos, scans, receipts, documents — are stored on our own server, not with a further provider.

Beyond those providers, data is seen by those who need it for their task: a club's officials see their members, a club's or an event's organisers its participants, lineups, waiver status and the licences of those working there, a treasurer the claims they decide, and the race committee the waiver scans of an event.
items: Hetzner Online GmbH, Gunzenhausen — the server that runs the website, its database and its files, in a data centre in Germany.
STRATO AG, Berlin — the mailbox and SMTP server used for outgoing mail.
sections.open: Whether a data processing agreement under Art. 28 GDPR exists with each of these providers has to be confirmed, and concluded where it is missing, before go-live.

sections.heading: Transfers to third countries
paragraphs: The website, its database and its files are run in Germany, and our mail goes out through a German provider; we do not transfer your data to a country outside the EU or the EEA.
The one exception is your own choice: signing in with Google or Microsoft is processing by that provider and may involve a transfer to the United States (see below).

sections.heading: How long we keep data
paragraphs: We delete personal data once the purpose it was collected for no longer applies, unless a statutory duty requires us to keep it longer — commercial and tax records, such as paid expense claims, have to be retained for up to ten years under German law.

You can delete your own account at any time. Its sign-in identities, roles, password, personal documents and bank account go with it, as do claims you never submitted. Your person record stays, unlinked from the account, because results, squads and waivers are part of the sporting record; submitted claims keep the name and IBAN they were paid to, for the books. An account removed by the administration is deactivated rather than erased.
sections.open: Concrete retention periods do not exist yet. Sign-in code records, the server's request log, the internal audit trail (which stores the acting person's email address), waiver confirmations and scans, receipts and uploaded photos are currently kept indefinitely, because no deletion routine has been built. A deletion concept with a period per category of data still has to be decided and implemented; until then this section cannot state exact periods.

sections.heading: Your rights
paragraphs: Under Arts. 15 to 21 GDPR you have the right to:

Write to vorstand@deutsche-segelliga.de to exercise any of them. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority, in particular in the Member State of your residence or your place of work, or where you believe the infringement took place.
items: access — confirmation of whether we process data about you, and a copy of that data;
rectification — correction of inaccurate data and completion of incomplete data;
erasure — deletion of your data, where no retention duty stands against it;
restriction of processing, as an alternative to erasure;
data portability — the data you provided, in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format;
objection — against processing based on legitimate interests, on grounds relating to your particular situation;
withdrawal of consent — at any time, without affecting the lawfulness of processing before the withdrawal.

sections.heading: Providing the site
paragraphs: To deliver the pages, your device's IP address is processed — technically unavoidable, since without it no response could reach you.

The server's request log records, for every request, your IP address, the time and the address requested. It serves troubleshooting and security only, is read by nobody else, and is never evaluated for any other purpose. There is no analytics, no advertising, no tracking pixel and no profiling of visitors anywhere on this website.
sections.open: The request log is not yet rotated: a short retention period — days, not months — has to be set before go-live.

sections.heading: Local storage instead of cookies
paragraphs: This site sets no cookies. It stores exactly two values in your browser's local storage:

Both are strictly necessary for functions you asked for, so no consent banner is required under § 25(2) TDDDG. Neither value is passed to third parties or used to recognise you across sites. If no language is stored, your browser's own language setting decides.
items: your access token, so that you stay signed in — removed when you sign out;
the interface language you chose.

sections.heading: Account and sign-in
paragraphs: An account holds your email address (stored in lower case), your display name, whether that address is verified, and the time of your last sign-in. Every account has exactly one person record; your clubs and roles hang off that, not off the account.

If you sign in with a code by email, we store the address, a hash of the code, its expiry, the number of attempts and whether it has been used. If you set a password, we store its Argon2id hash, when it was last changed, and the number of failed attempts and any lock that followed; setting, changing and removing it are logged without the password. After a successful sign-in, your browser holds an access token valid for twelve hours; it is not stored on our servers.
sections.open: Used and expired sign-in code records are currently not purged. A short deletion period — days, not years — should be set and implemented.

sections.heading: Signing in with Google or Microsoft
paragraphs: If you choose this route, you sign in at Google or Microsoft, and we receive an identity token from them which we verify. From that token we read and store only three things: your email address, the provider's permanent identifier for you, and your name.

To check the token's signature our server fetches the provider's public keys; no data about you is sent to the provider by us. Your use of the provider's own sign-in service is nevertheless processing by that provider, under its own privacy policy, and may involve a transfer to the United States. If you would rather avoid that, use the email code instead — it leads to the same account.

sections.heading: Club membership and roles
paragraphs: Membership of a club is a record the club's admin writes: which club it concerns, that you are a member, and when it was written. You can end it yourself at any time. Every such record, and its deletion, is logged with the acting account and the time.
Your email address is visible to your club's leadership and to the administration, not to other members. Fellow members see your display name and whether you are an organiser.

sections.heading: Sailor profiles, publication and results
paragraphs: A sailor record holds first and last name, date of birth, optionally an email address that links the profile to an account, and a federation number where one is on file.

Publicly — that is, without any sign-in — only name and role are shown, together with the club, the squads and the matchdays a person took part in. Email address, date of birth and federation number are never published.
Standings and results are recorded per team, not per person. Names become part of the public record through squad and lineup lists.
sections.open: The names of participants under 18 are published in exactly the same way as an adult's. Whether that should stay this way, and on what basis, needs legal review — as does whether a person should be able to object to publication of their name without leaving the competition.

sections.heading: Profile photos and the protection of minors
paragraphs: A photo can only be uploaded by the sailor themselves, from their own verified account, and they can delete it again at any time. It is scaled, cropped to a square and re-encoded, which removes the original metadata — including any location the camera recorded.

An adult's photo is publicly visible, unless they switched their profile page off. A minor's photo is not: it is served only to that person themselves, to the administration, and to the managers of the clubs the person is a member of. Everyone else is refused, including a signed-in stranger.
Age is determined from the date of birth on the record, with 18 as the threshold. Without a date of birth, a photo is protected as a minor's.

sections.heading: Liability waivers
paragraphs: When a waiver is confirmed for a series or an event, we keep a record of that confirmation as evidence. The record is not altered afterwards; a corrected waiver is a new confirmation. It holds:

People under 18 cannot confirm a waiver for themselves. Either a guardian signs the printed form and its scan is uploaded, or a parent whom the child's club linked to the child as guardian accepts online from their own account. No IP address is stored with a confirmation.
A scan is seen only by the sailor, the managers of their clubs, the event's organisers and race committee, and the administration — and every single look at it is logged.
items: which sailor, and which exact version of the waiver text;
the time of the confirmation and the language the text was shown in;
whether it was confirmed online, by a guardian online, or by a guardian on paper;
which account recorded it, and the browser identifier it was submitted from;
for minors: the guardian's name and, for a paper form, the scan.
sections.open: How long confirmations and scans are kept is undecided; a deletion deadline after the end of the season has to be set.

sections.heading: Expense claims and bank details
paragraphs: Whoever works at an event or is a member of a club can claim expenses. A claim holds its items (travel, accommodation, other costs), the receipts uploaded with it, and the decision on it with its date and note. When it is submitted, the name and IBAN of your saved bank account are copied onto it, so that a later change does not alter a claim already decided.

Your saved bank account is read by you alone. A claim, its receipts and the IBAN on it are seen by you and by those who decide it — the event's manager or treasurer, or the club's treasurer; looking at someone else's receipt is logged. The payment goes to the bank as a SEPA file the treasurer uploads to the club's online banking; the file is generated when downloaded and not stored, and we never log in to a bank.

sections.heading: Personal documents
paragraphs: You can upload your licences and certificates — boat licences, radio certificate, first aid, jury or race officer licence — with an expiry date, so that you need not send them again for every event.

They are seen by you, by the managers of the clubs you are a member of, and by the managers of the events you work at. Every look by someone other than you is logged. An expired document is marked, not deleted.

sections.heading: Emails we send
paragraphs: The website sends exactly one kind of email: sign-in and confirmation codes. There is no newsletter, no marketing and no notification mail. Every mail says why it was sent and whom to write to.
Mail goes out through our mailbox provider's SMTP server. The recipient address appears in the operating log for as long as that log is kept.

sections.heading: Log data and the internal audit trail
paragraphs: The server's request log records the IP address, time and address of each request (see “Providing the site”); the operating log records the recipient address of each email sent.

Changes — to memberships, roles, waivers, claims and payments, for instance — and every look at a waiver scan or at someone else's receipt or document are written to an internal audit trail together with the email address of the account that acted, so that they can be traced afterwards. It stores no IP address.
sections.open: The audit trail has no retention limit and is never pruned. A period has to be set for it.

sections.heading: Planned: position data from participants' phones
paragraphs: Live tracking of the boats using participants' own phones is planned. It is not built: today no position data is collected, stored or transmitted.

When it is built, it will process a device identifier, a timestamp, latitude, longitude, speed and heading during a race, and pass them to the timing and analysis system used for the league. Position data is movement data and can reveal considerably more than a race track — it will therefore rest on your explicit consent, given per event and revocable, and will never be switched on silently.
sections.open: The deletion concept for position data, the exact wording of the consent in the tracker, and how long tracks may be kept for replays are all still open. They must be settled before the feature is switched on; nothing in this policy should be read as approval for it. Before it is switched on, a data protection impact assessment (Art. 35 GDPR) is due — and with it, under § 38 (1) BDSG, a data protection officer.

sections.heading: Imports, exports and editorial content
paragraphs: Results, clubs and teams are imported from the league's scoring and from Manage2Sail. These imports carry clubs, team names, sail numbers and results — no names of sailors. A notice board links to the documents Manage2Sail publishes; we do not copy them.

The editorial team publishes news, press releases and pictures. A post names its author as written; a picture names its photographer. Photographers can deliver pictures through an upload link without an account; we store only the credit they are published under. Whoever publishes a photograph of an identifiable person has to make sure the necessary consent exists.
sections.open: A takedown route for a photo or a post someone objects to has to be settled. Sending results to an external timing and analysis system is planned and not active.

sections.heading: Current state of operation
paragraphs: This website is still being built. A test instance may hold demonstration data, and offer a development sign-in that issues access tokens without verification.
Real personal data should not be entered into an instance where that sign-in is switched on.
sections.open: The development sign-in has to be switched off before real accounts, sailors or waivers are entered. This section is expected to disappear at go-live.

sections.heading: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: We adapt this policy when the website changes. While new features are still being added — position tracking and the invitation of club members by mail in particular — it will keep changing; the date at the top tells you which version you are reading.

sections.heading: Terms used here
paragraphs: Briefly, and without the legal detail:
items: Personal data — any information relating to an identifiable person: a name, an email address, or a position on the water alike.
Processing — anything done with such data: collecting, storing, showing, transmitting, deleting.
Controller — whoever decides why and how data is processed; here, Deutsche Segel-Liga e.V.
Processor — a service provider that processes data on the controller's instructions, such as the hosting or mail provider.
Data subject — the person the data is about; you.
